- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp spike in price (true outcome > 3x recent mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 2x recent peak for next 7 days.  
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., +1.00 to -0.33 within 3 days), model fails to adjust; apply mean reversion to forecast by 5–15% toward recent 7-day average.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment; use 14-day rolling average to smooth forecast, especially if sentiment is volatile.  
- If true outcome shows sudden divergence from forecast (e.g., >1.5x deviation), check sentiment history for “reversal” signals (e.g., -0.33 followed by +1.00) — adjust forecast downward if sentiment shifts from bullish to neutral.
